en: Public blockchains can't check who qualifies without exposing who you are. JustEnough fixes that on Midnight.
Today a grant or an airdrop either collects ID documents, or gets farmed. LayerZero flagged over eight hundred thousand addresses as potential sybils, and only after the fact.
With JustEnough, your credential stays on your device. From your claim, the chain learns two facts: you are eligible, and it is your first claim.
This is the live demo. The compiled Compact circuits run right in your browser, with no wallet. The scenario is a Web3 community grant.
An issuer vouches for applicant A once. Only a salted hash goes on the ledger. The values stay on A's device.
The grant's rule is public: age nineteen to thirty-four, lives in Seoul, enrolled student. One grant per person.
A checks every condition on their own device,
and applies. On the right is what the chain sees: one receipt, called a nullifier. A live scan of the public data finds none of A's private values.
Applying twice gives the same nullifier, so the circuit refuses. The grant still doesn't know who tried.
Applicant B is not enrolled. Submitting anyway fails: no proof can be made.
Rewriting the value to enrolled fails too. The hash no longer matches anything the issuer published.
At closing, the operator reveals a draw seed it committed before anyone applied. Anyone can recompute who won.
Only a selected holder can claim. Nobody else's data ever reached the program.
The same flow ran on a local Midnight network with real zero-knowledge proofs: eight transactions, and zero attribute values in the public state.
Under the hood: one Compact contract with six circuits, one hundred and twelve automated tests, and CI on every push.
Try it without a wallet, at the link below. JustEnough. Prove you qualify, not who you are.
